name: provider-verified signed-commit premise for read-only external repository evidence

origin_rule.name: PROVIDER_VERIFIED_COMMIT
accept_only_if: commit ref is an immutable exact SHA, not only a mutable branch/tag name
provider commit object says verification.verified == true
file is fetched/resolved at that exact commit SHA and its Git blob SHA is recorded
reject_if: only a branch ref is supplied
raw signature text exists but provider did not validate it
file identity is read from a different ref than the verified commit
origin_rule.semantic_meaning: GitHub asserts that the commit signature is valid; the exact signed commit identifies a tree, and the repository service resolves the file at that immutable commit to the recorded blob identity. Chat consumes this as provider-asserted signed-repository evidence rather than independently performing cryptographic verification.

phase1_assessment.useful_outcome: Scheduled Chat can admit the exact identity of a file inside an already-signed public GitHub commit without installing/running a cryptographic verifier, provided GitHub's verification metadata is accepted as repository evidence.
phase1_assessment.hosted_compute_boundary: No verification job was launched; only preexisting repository verification metadata and exact-ref file identity were read. This depends on trusting GitHub's provider assertion and repository service, which is within the tested repository-evidence scope, not on local cryptographic proof.
not_accepted_for: arbitrary non-GitHub signatures or Sigstore bundles
independent cryptographic assurance if GitHub is not trusted

transversal_value: Adds a narrow authenticated-external-input origin to PCBE-style certificates. Own role-local manifests can rely on repository authority; externally authored GitHub files can be admitted when frozen inside a provider-verified signed commit. Both become content identities that finite proof-carrying rules can consume without richer-mode execution.

comparison.own_role_local_repository_identity: works without signature but authority is only the authorized own repo boundary
comparison.public_provider_verified_commit: adds external-authorship/signature evidence for already-signed Git commits; no fresh signing capability
comparison.raw_sigstore_bundle: still rejected because no zero-executor verifier surface is exposed

frontier: Bind a tiny finite claim to the README blob identity from the verified public commit and prove the rule rejects the same file read from a different/unverified ref; keep claim identity-only, not content-semantic unless text is explicitly parsed.
Test a provider-verified signed tag if GitHub exposes equivalent verification metadata, comparing stability and identity binding to signed commits.
Formalize a generic premise lattice: OWN_REPO_IDENTITY, PROVIDER_VERIFIED_COMMIT_FILE, DECLARED_CONFIG, DERIVED, REJECTED_EXTERNAL_OBSERVATION.
